newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Fewer crimes reported in Russia, clear-up rate up.
newsitem.headline: Fewer crimes reported in Russia, clear-up rate up.

text.p: Nearly two million crimes were reported in Russia during the first nine months of this year, fewer than last year, and the clear-up rate improved despite a lack of funds, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Monday.
"We had 4.5 percent fewer registered crimes than in the same period last year but we think this figure is still too high and serious crimes predominate," Kulikov told a news conference.
Drug-related offences were on the increase and about one third of registered crimes were committed by people under the influence of alcohol, he added.

Police solved about 1.4 million crimes in the nine month period -- 86,000 more than last year, Kulikov said. He added that his ministry had received only about 80 percent of its planned budget this year, already only half of its actual requirements.
The number of serious crimes in the Moscow region dropped by 20 percent in the nine-month period against the previous year.
"Life has become calmer, street crime has declined in most cities," Kulikov said.
But corruption in the interior ministry remains a big problem, with 73,000 employees dismissed for "negative behaviour" and 600 police officers facing trial on charges of corruption, he added.
